# Jubilees Chapter 6 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 6:1 — "tents of Shem" vs. "dwelling-places of Shem"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "may God dwell in the dwelling-places of Shem" | Literal Ge'ez construction |
| LOGOS | "May God dwell in the tents of Shem" | Echoes Gen 9:27; "tents" is idiomatic |
| PNEUMA | "May God make his home in Shem's tents" | Same as LOGOS, slightly colloquial |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "tents of Shem." This deliberately echoes Gen 9:27 (LXX: "in the tents of Shem"); "dwelling-places" (EMET) is accurate but loses the echo.

---

## 6:4 — "sweet savour" vs. "sweet fragrance" vs. "sweet smell"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sweet-savour" / "sweet savour" (hyphenated) | Literal technical cultic term |
| LOGOS | "sweet-smelling offering" / "sweet fragrance" | Standard cultic term in formal register |
| PNEUMA | "fragrant offering" / "sweet smell" | Natural modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "sweet-smelling offering" / "sweet fragrance." "Sweet savour" (EMET) is archaic but precise; "sweet fragrance" is the formal modern equivalent of the cultic term reyha besam. PNEUMA's "sweet smell" is too casual for cultic context.

---

## 6:20 — "afflict themselves" vs. "humble themselves"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to fast and to afflict themselves" | Literal Ge'ez; "afflict" = standard Yom Kippur idiom |
| LOGOS | "to fast and to humble themselves" | "Humble themselves" is standard English liturgical idiom |
| PNEUMA | "to fast, to humble themselves" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "humble themselves." Both are valid translations of the Ge'ez verb; "humble themselves" is the established liturgical rendering (cf. Lev 16:29 in translation tradition) and preferred in formal context.

---

## 6:26 — Calendar statement: repeated "three hundred and sixty-four"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the whole number of the days of this year is three hundred and sixty-four days...three hundred and sixty-four" | Repeats number as in source |
| LOGOS | Same — the repetition is in the Ge'ez | Preserves the emphasis |
| PNEUMA | "Three hundred and sixty-four days — a complete year, no more, no less" | Condenses to remove repetition |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The repetition of "three hundred and sixty-four" in the source is deliberate emphasis — this is Jubilees' foundational calendrical assertion. PNEUMA's "no more, no less" is vivid but editorializes.

---

## 6:31 — "eat all the blood with all flesh" vs. "eat blood with meat"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they will eat of all the blood with all flesh" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "they will eat all manner of blood with all manner of flesh" | Formal, preserves "all manner of" |
| PNEUMA | "they will eat blood with their meat" | Colloquial compression |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "All manner of blood with all manner of flesh" preserves the comprehensiveness of the Ge'ez formulation. PNEUMA's "their meat" is too casual and loses the scope.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
